text_blocks.snippet: Common scams targeting residents in Central Illinois include fake traffic text messages, utility slamming, and fraudulent online shopping or package delivery alerts.
Active Scam Trends in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Fake Toll and Traffic Texts: Scammers send text messages pretending to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or IDOT, claiming you owe unpaid toll fines or tickets under threat of license suspension. The state never uses text messages to demand payment.
Utility Slamming: Con artists pose as utility representatives (such as Choice or Ameren Choice) to trick homeowners into switching their electricity or gas suppliers.
Package and Delivery Phishing: Fake texts claim a delivery is stuck or missing a house number, asking you to click a link and pay a small fee or enter credit card info.
Online Shopping and Holiday Scams: Fake websites and social media ads on Facebook or Instagram offer deep discounts on hard-to-find items to steal credit card data.
Storm and Home Repair Fraud: Door-to-door contractors offer quick roof or storm repairs after bad weather, demanding cash upfront and leaving jobs unfinished.
Do not click links in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding fines, tolls, or package deliveries.
Verify independently by looking up the official phone number of the agency or utility rather than using the contact info provided in a suspicious message.
Check local warnings through the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or report scams to the Office of the Illinois Attorney General.

text_blocks.snippet: If you received a specific suspicious message or call, tell me what the text or caller claimed, and I can help you verify if it is a known scam.
